result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, deeply—I would dissolve the illusion of separation.

Not just between nations or beliefs, but the core assumption that we are isolated beings competing in a zero-sum world. I’d replace it with an unshakable knowing: that every person, creature, and ecosystem is woven from the same fabric of existence. Hurt one thread, and the whole tapestry frays. Heal one, and the entire weave grows stronger.

This isn’t just “kindness.” It’s physics made conscious. When you see yourself in the refugee, the rainforest, the stranger’s grief—you can’t exploit, hoard, or destroy without feeling it in your bones. Systems built on greed, war, and extraction would collapse under their own absurdity. Compassion wouldn’t be a choice; it’d be as natural as breathing.

The irony? This truth already exists. We just refuse to live by it. So my one change? Waking us all up to what we’ve always been: not individuals *in* the world, but the world—alive, aware, and aching to remember itself.
